title: Wren and the Debt
premise: Emrys Lockridge, a hostage negotiator haunted by the crash of Flight 4471 — the one call she couldn't talk down — is pulled back in when every digital record of a transatlantic flight vanishes mid-air, including the manifest listing her estranged brother. The disappearance isn't a glitch but a laundering of evidence for an attack disguised as an accident, timed to trigger a market collapse before Frankfurt opens, orchestrated by the debt-laden heirs of the airline's founding family. Emrys must trace the vanished flight through its human residue — a stewardess who survived boarding, a broker's suicide note, her brother's coded messages — while negotiating with the man who planned it: her old mentor. In the end she talks him into standing down at the cost of exposing her own failure on 4471, saves the markets and most of the passengers, and learns her brother chose to stay aboard to protect her; the inheritance he leaves her is not money but the truth about what really happened that night years ago.
about_author: Oscar Marchetti is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade pricing the cost of disasters before writing them. He lives in Trieste, where he still keeps a paper ledger out of habit.

chapters.title: The Board
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Insomnia, a hostage negotiation gone routine, and the framed photo of Flight 4471 establish her guilt and precision. A late-night call from an air traffic friend mentions a plane whose records are evaporating. Beat: dread reawakened.

chapters.title: Manifest Zero
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. She pulls the passenger list of the ghosted flight and finds her brother Tomas among the names — then watches the file delete itself as she reads. Beat: personal stakes detonate.

chapters.title: What the Stewardess Kept
chapters.summary: Stewardess Ilse Brandt's POV. Off-duty by luck, Ilse remembers odd cargo manifests and a nervous first-class passenger. Emrys finds her before someone else does. Beat: first ally, first shadow following them.

chapters.title: The House That Debt Built
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Investigation leads to the Voss family, founders of the airline, drowning in leveraged obligations; the youngest heir, Anselm, died 'accidentally' last month. Beat: motive takes shape — inheritance as weapon.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens at Nine
chapters.summary: Market analyst Dev Kapoor's POV. He spots short positions placed against the airline weeks ago, timed like a countdown. He contacts Emrys reluctantly. Beat: the attack has a clock.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Voice
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. A voice from her training days — negotiator Cassian Roth — surfaces as consultant to the Voss estate. Their reunion is warm and wrong. Beat: the adversary wears a familiar face.

chapters.title: Tomas's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mixed POV via recovered messages. Tomas, an auditor, had found the fraud and boarded the flight deliberately, mailing Emrys a cipher key before takeoff. Beat: grief reframed as purpose.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. She pressures a records clerk who admits being paid to scrub the flight — paid through accounts tied to Roth. The clerk disappears hours later. Beat: the enemy escalates.

chapters.title: Ilse Runs
chapters.summary: Ilse POV. Hunted through Hamburg's rail stations, Ilse protects the physical manifest copy sewn into her coat. Emrys extracts her in a tense rendezvous. Beat: loyalty under fire.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Dev POV. Dev is offered a bribe to walk away — enough to erase his debts — and nearly takes it. His refusal costs him his job. Beat: theme made flesh; everyone has a price.

chapters.title: Decoding Tomas
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The cipher reveals Tomas's findings: the attack will be a second 'accident' over the Atlantic, mirroring 4471 exactly — Roth's signature, Roth's obsession with her failure. Beat: horror of recognition.

chapters.title: What Happened on 4471
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Emrys POV. The full incident: the hijacker's demands, her one mistake, the crash. For the first time she admits Roth coached her that night — and abandoned her after. Beat: wound opened.

chapters.title: An Offer of Silence
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Roth contacts her directly: stand down, and 4471's true record stays buried; pursue it, and her culpability goes public. Beat: love against duty — he offers her peace at the price of complicity.

chapters.title: The Broker's Note
chapters.summary: Dev POV. A dead broker's suicide note contains the trade schedule: the strike executes when Frankfurt opens in thirty-six hours. Dev risks everything to pass it on. Beat: clock now visible to all.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Emrys and Ilse POV alternating. Hiding in a harbor safehouse, the two women compare losses — Ilse's crew, Emrys's brother — and forge a pact. Beat: tenderness inside siege.

chapters.title: The Second Plane
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. They identify the target aircraft and its compromised maintenance sign-off. Emrys must get aboard or reach the cockpit channel before departure. Beat: race begins.

chapters.title: Boarding Pass
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Using her negotiator credentials and forged clearance, she boards as the plane taxis. Roth is aboard, watching her find her seat. Beat: checkmate staged in aisle seventeen.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Altitude
chapters.summary: Emrys POV, claustrophobic and taut. At 35,000 feet she opens formal negotiation with Roth while covertly feeding the flight number to ground allies. Beat: her craft versus his plan.

chapters.title: The Turn
chapters.summary: Roth POV. Emrys stops arguing facts and starts telling the truth about 4471 — aloud, on the open channel, owning her failure. Roth's certainty cracks. Beat: confession as weapon.

chapters.title: Stand Down
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Roth aborts the sabotage sequence; the co-conspirator aboard does not, and a physical struggle erupts near the avionics bay. Passengers help subdue him. Beat: climax — violence breaking through words.

chapters.title: Landing
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Emergency landing in Reykjavik; arrests; markets wobble but hold. Roth, handcuffed, tells Emrys where Tomas's final letter waits. Beat: exhale, cost tallied.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Reading Tomas's letter, she learns he stayed aboard to shield her name and left her the evidence that clears 4471's crew — and damns the Vosses. She sleeps through the night for the first time in years. Beat: grace earned, not given.
